mdz_immediate_pdf.page_mapping: PDF page 1 is an MDZ-generated bibliographic cover; PDF pages 2-165 map one-to-one and in order to IIIF canvases 1-164.

observations: Canvas 1 is the BSB binding and canvas 2 carries the holding call number Ph.pr. 881 kc.
Canvas 5 is the historical title page: Götzen-Dämmerung oder Wie man mit dem Hammer philosophirt, Friedrich Nietzsche, Leipzig, Verlag von C. G. Naumann, 1889.
No edition statement is displayed on the title or rights leaf.
Canvases 9-11 contain the Vorwort, canvas 13 contains the contents, and canvas 15 begins printed page 1.
Canvases 150-154 continue printed pages 136-140; canvas 154 closes the preceding section.
Canvas 155 begins Der Hammer redet; canvases 157-158 carry printed pages 143-144 and complete the work.
Canvas 159 is blank, canvas 160 is a Naumann advertisement, and canvas 164 is the rear binding.

scholarly_text_history.source: Andreas Urs Sommer, Historischer und kritischer Kommentar zu Friedrich Nietzsches Werken, Band 6/1
bounded_findings: Nietzsche sent the manuscript to Naumann on 7 September 1888 and continued title, proof, and content changes.
Printing was completed on 13 November 1888 and Nietzsche received four finished copies on 24 November.
The 1889-dated work became available in bookshops at the end of January 1889.
Köselitz's 1893 second edition altered headings and text; the exact 1889 item must not be flattened into that edition.
